artifacts.summary: 3-phase implementation: f->z pure relabel, BX_c/TM_c redefined as BX_r/TM_r extending BX_d/TM_d with R-time semantics, section 2/5 leansrc citation swap fixed, Naming provenance remark rewritten. All gates pass.

completion_data.completion_summary: Aligned typst frame-class subscripts (f/d/c -> z/d/r) with the paper's current def:BX-z/-d/-r naming in typst/FormalFoundations.typ and typst/chapters/p2-decidability-practice.typ, redefined BX_r/TM_r as an extension of BX_d/TM_d (R-time only, matching Lean's soundness_rtime), fixed a swapped #leansrc citation pair between the section 2 Soundness theorem and section 5 Algebraic soundness proposition, and rewrote the Naming provenance remark. All 3 plan phases completed; typst compile (both documents), typst-sync-check.sh, and check-paper-definitions.sh all pass.

memory_candidates.content: When a typst prose claim asserts a formal system's semantic class (e.g. 'sound over Dur = RR' / 'a class containing a dense or RR member'), verify it directly against the Lean theorem's typeclass binders (e.g. [DenselyOrdered F.Duration] plus a BddAbove/IsLUB hypothesis for Dedekind-completeness) rather than trusting the prose or the plan's paraphrase. This caught/confirmed that Lean's soundness_rtime genuinely requires dense AND Dedekind-complete (R-time), matching the paper's def:BX-r redefinition as an extension of BX_d rather than a bare 'complete' class.

scripts/check-paper-definitions.sh distinguishes a 'pass' (whole-file checksum drifted, e.g. from an unrelated live-tree edit, but every individually-recorded definition's own checksum is unchanged) from a genuine drift failure. A live-tree checksum notice in its output is not automatically a neutral-skip or a blocker -- read the per-definition-count line to confirm 'all N recorded definitions are unchanged -- pass' before treating the gate as failed or skipped.
